newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-AUSTRALIAN SPORTS NEWS - AUGUST 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-AUSTRALIAN SPORTS NEWS - AUGUST 11.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian runner Steve Moneghetti came third in the world championship marathon in Greece yesterday since first trying to pick up a medal in 1987. He will use his prize money to bid for Raelene Boyle's silver medal, and plans to return it to her. Page 2.

Australian swimmers Shelley Taylor-Smith and Grant Robinson broke the world records for their respective events in the 25 kilometre openwater swims at the Pan Pacific championships in Japan yesterday, despite competing in post-typhoon conditions. Page 25.

The Sydney Swans allowed St Kilda to come back from a 38 point margin to win their Australian Football League clash 17.17 (119) to 18.20 (128) yesterday, bringing the Swans' streak of 20 consecutive wins at the Sydney Cricket Ground to an end. Page 27.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Super League operations manager Graham Annesley yesterday sympathised with Australian Rugby League referees director Michael Stone over the pressure from coaches and commentators to introduce a video referee for the finals games. Page 24.

The Brisbane Broncos secured the Super League minor premiership yesterday despite being without star players Allan Langer and Glenn Lazarus, when they trounced Penrith 54-12 in front of 14,000 people at ANZ Stadium. Page 24.

The Australian Crocs men's under-23 basketball team has won the world championships with an 88-73 win over Puerto Rico in Melbourne last night. The win is only the second time a basketball title has been won by an Australian team. Page 26.
THE AGE

Geelong coach Gary Ayres will ask the Australian Football League to give clarification on an umpire's decision to call a touched behind from a set shot which may have cost Geelong the match against Essendon at the Melbourne Cricket Ground yesterday. Page .

Collingwood coach Tony Shaw yesterday questioned whether he was getting through to his players and indicated he might leave next year if the Magpies did not improve next season, after the team looks set to miss the Australian Football League finals for th third year in a row. Page 6.

The National Basketball League is heading for its closest finish ever with unexpected wins by Townsville and the Melbourne Tigers at the weekend meaning only two wins separate the seven teams behind competition leader South East Melbourne. Page 20.
THE HERALD SUN

Martin Craggill achieved a first and second place in the two heats of the fourth round of the Australian Superbike Championship in Brisbane yesterday, advancing from fifth place on the points table to second, just 16 behind leader Troy Bayliss. Page 85.

Twenty-four year old Queenslander Joanna Stone threw a personal best distance of 68.64 metres in the women's javelin at the world championships in Greece yesterday, taking out the silver medal, falling only 14 centimetres short of the gold medal winning distance. age 84.

Defending champions New South Wales defeated Victoria 1-0 last night at the state hockey centre in a game that saw Victoria, playing at home, end their national women's hockey league season at the bottom of the competition ladder. Page 78.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Victorian swimmer Michael Klim came from half a second behind in the 200 metre freestyle event to pass American champion Josh Davis and win a gold medal at the Pan Pacific swimming championships in Japan last night. Page 29.

Paul Morris, the 1995 champion, extended his championship lead by 13 points in the fifth round of the Australian two-litre motor racing series at Winton yesterday, after defending champion, second-placed Geoff Brabham, was knocked out of the first race. Pge 29.

The Perth Reds defeated the Hunter Mariners 30-22 in the Super League match at the WACA yesterday, giving the team a slim chance of making the semi-finals, while the Mariners missed the opportunity to move into the top five. Page 36.
